messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

you should be able to use your tables given they are in the correct format.

The minimum requirements for the recordTable are: Station ID, species ID, Date/Time (in other words, where was which species seen at which time?).

For the camera trap table, station ID (also camera ID if > 1 camera per station), setup and retrieval date are required. If cameras malfunctioned during the survey, also two columns specifying those periods can be supplied.

Station IDs must match between the two tables, and the station column name of both tables must match too.

More details on the latter are here:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/ImageOrganisation.html#camera-trap-station-information

The file paths are merely for information purposes, to know which image an entry in the table refers to.

Best regards,

Jürgen

messages.subject: detectionHistory problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jurgen,

I'm trying to generate species detection histories for the different stations. Unfortunately when I ran this the output always show the entire data set and not the stations I've chosen.
Here I'm following the script from the vignette and using StationA as the example. Please have a look at it and help me identify the problem. Thanks.

station.a <- recordTableSample[recordTableSample$Station == "StationA", ]
DetHist1 <- detectionHistory(recordTable         = station.a,
                            camOp                = camop_no_problem,
                            stationCol           = "Station",
                            speciesCol           = "Species",
                            recordDateTimeCol    = "DateTimeOriginal",
                            species              = "PBE",
    timeZone             = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur",                                                                                                                    occasionLength       = 1,
                            day1                 = "2015-05-11",
                            includeEffort        = TRUE,
    scaleEffort          = FALSE)

dh <- DetHist1$detection_history[1,]
View(dh)

messages.subject: Re: detectionHistory problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
the detection history function combines two data sources:
- the record table, with record date, time, ID, and location
- the camera operation matrix which contains information about what cameras were used,

but you only subsetted one of them.

By subsetting the record table you basically say there were no more records, but the information about what stations were available (the camera operation matrix) remains unchanged.
What you need to do here is subset the camera operation table too, e.g.

camop_no_problem[rownames(camop_no_problem) == "StationA",]

messages.subject: can't extract metadata
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I would like to use CamtrapR to solely extract exif metadata from my images. I'm not sure why I can't recognize the JPEGs which are in the 'wild_photos2015' folder:

setwd("/Users/MZ/Desktop/camera/wild_photos2015")
wd_images_ID <- system.file("camera/wild_photos2015", package = "camtrapR")

upon:
length(list.files(wd_images_ID))
I receive:
[1] 0

Similarly:
exifTagNames(inDir = wd_images_ID, returnMetadata = TRUE)
I receive:
Error: file.exists(inDir) is not TRUE

Do I need to rename my pictures first or use different directory names? (My images are in JPEG format and I did download ExifTool). Thanks very much.

Thanks very much for any advice.

messages.subject: Re: can't extract metadata
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
The  system.file() command is only used to find the sample data included in the package. You don't need this for your own data. The specify the directory containing the images, do this (I guess youare on a Mac):

wd_images_ID <- "/Users/MZ/Desktop/camera/wild_photos2015"

If you use Windows, you'd have to specify the drive letter too, e.g.:

wd_images_ID <- "C:/Users/MZ/Desktop/camera/wild_photos2015"

Best regards,
Jürgen
